Package org.opencastproject.util

Class GsonUtil

java.lang.Object
org.opencastproject.util.GsonUtil
public final class GsonUtil extends Object
Provides the Gson instance Opencast uses for reading and writing JSON.

Gson's defaults are unsuitable for Opencast in four ways, which is why this shared instance exists instead of every call site building its own:

  • By default Gson escapes <, >, &, = and ' as \\uXXXX. Opencast serializes URLs almost everywhere, so this would litter the output with escapes.
  • By default Gson omits object members whose value is null. The External API explicitly requires empty fields to be present, so they have to be serialized.
  • By default Gson reads every JSON number into a Double when the target type is unknown, which silently loses precision for large integers. LONG_OR_DOUBLE keeps integral values as Long.
  • By default Gson parses leniently and accepts input the JSON specification does not allow, such as unquoted keys, single quotes or comments. Parsing is set to strict so that only valid JSON is accepted. Note that this is stricter than json-simple was, which tolerated unescaped control characters in strings and trailing commas.

Gson is thread safe, so the single instance can be shared freely.

    • parse

      public static com.google.gson.JsonElement parse(String json)
      Parses a JSON document into a tree, using the same strict rules as gson().

      Use this instead of JsonParser.parseString(String), which always parses leniently. Like parseString, an empty document is returned as JsonNull.

      Parameters:
      json - the JSON document
      Returns:
      the parsed JSON tree
      Throws:
      com.google.gson.JsonSyntaxException - if the input is not valid JSON

    • getStringOrNull

      public static String getStringOrNull(com.google.gson.JsonObject json, String key)
      Reads a string member from a JSON object.

      json-simple returned null from get() for an absent key and for an explicit JSON null alike, and the surrounding code was written against that. Gson distinguishes the two and answers with a JsonNull in the second case, which JsonElement.getAsString() would then fail on. This collapses both back to null.

      Parameters:
      json - the object to read from
      key - the member name
      Returns:
      the member as a string, or null if it is absent or JSON null

    • getObjectOrNull

      public static com.google.gson.JsonObject getObjectOrNull(com.google.gson.JsonObject json, String key)
      Reads an object member from a JSON object.

      Like getStringOrNull(JsonObject, String), this treats an absent key and an explicit JSON null alike. JsonObject.getAsJsonObject(String) would fail on the latter.

      Parameters:
      json - the object to read from
      key - the member name
      Returns:
      the member as an object, or null if it is absent or JSON null
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the member is not an object

    • asText

      public static String asText(com.google.gson.JsonElement value)
      Renders a JSON value as plain text.

      json-simple handed back bare Java objects, so toString() on a parsed member gave the string itself. A JsonElement's toString() is its JSON text, which would wrap a string in quotes. This returns the raw string for primitives and the JSON text for objects and arrays, matching the old behaviour.

      Parameters:
      value - the value to render
      Returns:
      the value as plain text

    • asText

      public static String asText(com.google.gson.JsonElement value, String fallback)
      Renders a JSON value as plain text like asText(JsonElement), falling back to a default for an absent member or JSON null.
      Parameters:
      value - the value to render, may be null
      fallback - the text to return if the value is null or JSON null
      Returns:
      the value as plain text, or the fallback

    • toStringMap

      public static Map<String,String> toStringMap(com.google.gson.JsonObject json)
      Flattens a JSON object into a map of strings.

      json-simple's object was a Map already, so callers used to cast it and read the values as strings. This renders each member with asText(JsonElement) and maps JSON null to null, as the cast did.

      Parameters:
      json - the object to flatten
      Returns:
      the members of the object as plain text
